learning_outcomes.text: Identify the fundamental elements of integral control of production and manufacturing processes in industry.
Define the necessary elements for the implementation of control systems for proposed cases.
Understand the operation of communication, supervision, and control systems for process optimization.
Apply appropriate methodologies for the implementation of the different elements of an integral control system.
Apply the appropriate norms and representation methods to the industrial control project.

syllabus_topics: CIM, the control pyramid in industry
Instrumentation in process and manufacturing control
Sensors: conventional and advanced (virtual sensors, vision systems, …)
Actuators: Valves, electric motors, pneumatics, hydraulics, robotics.
Devices for process and sequential system control: PID, PLC, microP, DSP, PC, …
Point-to-point communications: Analog and digital signal transmitters.
Security in communications and information systems
Supervision and control at plant level
Data exploitation techniques: data representation, statistical treatment, data mining.
Methodologies for the development of automated systems
Normative for the design of batch manufacturing ISA S88 (IEC 61512-01)
Integration of enterprise control systems ISA S95
Integration of information technologies: MES, WMS, TMS, ERP
Design and development standards ISA 5.1, 5.5 and UNE
assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 is required on the Final Exam and the Practical Work. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.8 x EF) + (0.2 x TP). Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0. In the extraordinary call, an exam (80%) and practical work (20%) are evaluated, with a minimum of 4 out of 10 required for each part. If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.8 x Theory) + (0.2 x Practical Work); otherwise, the grade will be the minimum between the calculated grade and 4.0.
